Running MTDI on a Raspberry Pi

MTDI Studio · October 2026

The M in MTDI stands for microprocessing: it should run where the data is, on small, slow, low-power computers.

What it needs

  • Python 3.9 or newer. The engine and every pillar except the interface use only the standard library.
  • For the browser interface: Dash and Flask (pip install -r requirements.txt). Inductra Vaion already ran a much heavier Dash interface on a Raspberry Pi 5.
  • For serial sources: pyserial.

How heavy it is

On the 2.1 GHz Xeon server used to develop it, the engine ingests a protocol line in about 25 µs and builds a full packet in about 2 ms, with about 15 MB resident. A Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W is roughly 10–20× slower per core. That is an estimate, not a measurement on a Pi, but it still puts Inductra's ~100 lines per second at a few percent of one core.

Lighter modes

python -m mtdi run projects/host-health --headless   # JSON API only, no Dash
python -m mtdi watch projects/host-health            # live view in the terminal, over SSH

Headless mode serves /mtdi/packet, /mtdi/state, /mtdi/ingest, /mtdi/action and /mtdi/ask, so a heavier machine (or MATLAB, through mtdi.packet) can draw the interface while the Pi only measures.

Start on boot

# /etc/systemd/system/mtdi.service
[Unit]
Description=MTDI Studio
After=network-online.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/home/pi/mtdi-studio
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m mtdi run projects/host-health --host 0.0.0.0
Restart=always
User=pi

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
sudo systemctl enable --now mtdi
